To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the problem of routing in hybrid networks is different from the problem of routing on wireless ad hoc networks and that it is not a simple extension of the latter, and that (ii) the problem of finding the best routing paths in hybrid networks is NP-hard.

(1) the performance of a routing protocol in a mobile ad hoc network depends on how the nodes move, and (2) the performance of any online protocol in the worst case is very poor, even if the network is not very sparse, and the geographic position and destination of a message are known.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How can we find good paths in hybrid networks even if we have no knowledge of network conditions?
the design of routing protocols for wireless ad hoc network that can cope with the worst case scenario.
the design and analysis of algorithms and protocols for wireless ad hoc and sensor networks.
